v01.title: Day 1
v01.author: R. Vance
v01.text: Relieved the summer crew at 14:10. Generator coughs when it's cold, breaker trips if you look at it. Hollis left the place tidy: mug on its hook, pencils sharpened. Dispatch says he walked out. Nobody walks anywhere out here. Logged the 20:00. The coffee tastes of diesel.

v02.title: Day 3
v02.author: R. Vance
v02.text: North mast reads 7 hPa under the south. The masts are 300 metres apart. That isn't weather, that's a fault. Sent it to Dispatch. Imogen said log it as read and don't recalibrate. Strange instruction from a weather service.

v03.title: Day 5
v03.author: R. Vance
v03.text: The fault only shows at night, and it moves. 4 hPa at 20:00. 11 at 02:00. Like something leaning on the north mast. Re-taped the window. The draught smells of salt, which makes no sense 200 km from open water.

v04.title: Day 6
v04.author: R. Vance
v04.text: Found Hollis's reading book under the bunk. Every page the same two columns, north and south. In the margin, every night at 03:00, a tally mark. Three strokes. Never four.

v05.title: Day 7
v05.author: R. Vance
v05.text: 03:00. Three knocks at the west door. I'm the only person for 400 km. I didn't open it. I'm writing this down so I remember that I didn't open it.

v06.title: Day 9
v06.author: R. Vance
v06.text: Tracks this morning, from the north mast straight to the west door. Boot prints, my size. I hadn't been out. The wind should have filled them by dawn. It hadn't.

v07.title: Day 10
v07.author: R. Vance
v07.text: Asked Imogen what happened to Hollis. She asked for the 22:00 reading. I asked again. She said the Service values continuity of the record. Then the line hissed and she was gone.

v08.title: Day 11
v08.author: R. Vance
v08.text: The drop has a rhythm. It deepens between 02:00 and 03:30 and lifts by dawn. Hollis's tallies sit on the same hours. He was logging the same thing. He just never wrote down what it was.

v09.title: Day 12
v09.author: R. Vance
v09.text: Moved my bunk into the generator room. It's louder and warmer and there's no window. You can't hear knocking over the generator. That's the point.

v10.title: Day 13
v10.author: R. Vance
v10.text: Four cans in the shed yesterday. Three this morning. I'm the only one here who drinks coffee, and the mug was on the table, not the hook. From now on I write down where I leave things.

v11.title: Day 14
v11.author: R. Vance
v11.text: Walked the tether out to the north mast like Imogen wanted. Halfway there I heard boots behind me in the snow, keeping step with mine. When I stopped, they stopped half a step late. I didn't turn round. North reads 12 under.

v12.title: Day 14, 02:10
v12.author: R. Vance
v12.text: Bedroll's between the drums now. I sleep two hours at a time between readings. Dreamed about the mast light. In the dream it was warm out there and I'd left the door open for someone.

v13.title: Day 15
v13.author: R. Vance
v13.text: Imogen asked if I'd been outside without the tether. I haven't. She said the north mast logged something at 03:10, thirty-seven degrees, standing still for an hour. Then she asked me to forget she'd said it.

v14.title: Day 15
v14.author: R. Vance
v14.text: Antenna iced again, third night running. Went out and knocked it clear. Coming back, there was a second set of prints beside mine. Same boots, longer stride. They went past the mast and kept going north. There's nothing north.

v15.title: Day 15, 04:10
v15.author: R. Vance
v15.text: Three cans. Mug on the hook. Bedroll rolled up. Tape on the window. Everything where I left it. Writing it down helps. If it's written down, I know which of us moved it.

v16.title: Day 16
v16.author: R. Vance
v16.text: Opened Hollis's footlocker. Under the socks there's a Service memo. KESTREL-4 ANOMALY PROGRAMME, PHASE 3. Keeper retention: 21 days average. Data quality: excellent. Recommend continued staffing. Initialled I. P.

v17.title: Day 16
v17.author: R. Vance
v17.text: Asked Imogen what Phase 3 is. Eleven seconds of silence. I timed it. Then: "Log the 22:00, Robert." I have never told her my first name.

v18.title: Day 17
v18.author: R. Vance
v18.text: There was one of Hollis's tapes behind the panel in my bunk room. I've played it four times. He sounds calm, and that's the worst part. He sounds like a man reading out a bus timetable.

v19.title: Day 17, 02:40
v19.author: R. Vance
v19.text: Dispatch called at 01:30. At 02:30 Dispatch called again to ask why I'd called her at 01:30. I hadn't. Both voices were Imogen's. Only one of them used the call sign.

v20.title: Day 17, 04:05
v20.author: R. Vance
v20.text: Taped my bunk room shut from the outside, so I'll know if the tape is ever torn. Everything I need is in the generator room now. For whoever comes next: it can't come in. It can only ask.

v21.title: Day 18
v21.author: R. Vance
v21.text: North minus south was 19 at 02:00. The barograph pen tore through the paper. The mast light was on when I went to bed and off when I woke up. The mast light doesn't have a switch.

v22.title: Day 18
v22.author: R. Vance
v22.text: At 03:00 Imogen's voice came from the west door. Not the radio. The door. She said the helicopter was down by the mast and said my name. The real Imogen is in Tromsø. I said so out loud, and it stopped.

v23.title: Day 19
v23.author: R. Vance
v23.text: I've worked it out. Hollis didn't walk out. He answered. Every keeper answers in the end, because it never asks for much. Just come and look. Only for a minute. Only to be sure.

v24.title: Day 19
v24.author: R. Vance
v24.text: If you're reading this, you're the next keeper, and the Service has told you I walked out. I want you to know I logged every reading. I want you to know the door is the one thing it can't open.

v25.title: Day 19, 02:58
v25.author: R. Vance
v25.text: It's using my voice now. That's how I know it's close. It sounds better than me. It sounds warm. The mast light's on. I'll log the 03:00, and then I'm going to look. Don't follow my tracks.
